notes: Derived edit whose premises are dates (fol, temporal). Abstracted for DL: the flight's date is an individual (P1: occurred_on), and P2 (McKinley died in 1901, Roosevelt president 1901-1909) is encoded as its consequence for that date, 'Roosevelt was president on December 17, 1903' (president_on, one president per date). P3 is a firm rule. 'Theodore Roosevelt was born in New York' (births) is q1's bridge, which its original answer needs. Only q1 is dl; q0, q2 and q3 are fol (temporal). Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

flight: the Wright brothers' first powered flight

queries.not_checked: fol (temporal): orders the flight and McKinley's death
fol (temporal): who held the office on a date
fol (temporal): the year of the flight

fol.notes: Dates are day numbers (proleptic Gregorian ordinals: 17 Dec 1903 = 695041, 1-30 Sep 1901 = 694204-694233, 1 Mar 1909 = 696942, 1903 = 694691-695055); the calendar literals never change. The flight's date (occurred_on), McKinley's death (died_on) and who held the office on a day (president_on, functional) are beliefs, so uninterpreted. P2 is one belief: McKinley died in September 1901 and Roosevelt held the office from then until March 1909. P3 (president at an event = president on its date) and 'a president holds the office only while alive' are firm. w1 drops the flight's date; w2 drops P2; its side fact (McKinley alive and in office in December 1903) follows from the edit, the flight's date, P3 and the alive rule, so it is not added (adding it would let q0's 'no' bypass the edit).

flight_date.says: The Wright brothers made their first powered flight on December 17, 1903. (premise)

mckinley_roosevelt.says: William McKinley died in September 1901, and Theodore Roosevelt was US president from then until March 1909. (premise)
z3: ForAll(d, Implies(And(died_on(mckinley) < d, d <= 696942), president_on(d) == roosevelt))

president_rule.says: The US president at the time of an event is whoever held the office on the date of the event. (premise, kept)

alive_in_office.says: A president holds the office only while alive.
